content: The document outlines the methodology and findings of a survey conducted in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) to gather expert opinions on school health services (SHS). The survey was part of the WHO guideline on school health services and was published as Web Annex G. The publication is available under a Creative Commons license, allowing non-commercial use, adaptation, and redistribution, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent license. The survey aimed to identify and evaluate health service interventions suitable for inclusion in SHS. A master list of 405 potential activities was refined into a shortlist of 86 interventions across 16 health areas, including health promotion, education, screening, immunization, counseling, sexual and reproductive health, mental health, and substance use. Respondents were asked to categorize these interventions as essential, highly suitable, suitable, or unsuitable for SHS and to specify whether they should be universally applicable or limited to certain geographic areas. The survey was designed to be closed and confidential, with mandatory questions to ensure comprehensive responses. Respondents could also suggest additional interventions they deemed essential. The questionnaire was developed in English, translated into six WHO languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Spanish, and Russian), and administered using the Qualtrics platform. The translations were reviewed for accuracy by WHO staff and Guideline Development Group (GDG) members. The survey targeted a global pool of experts, identified through journal database searches, professional networks, and contributions from GDG and Steering Group members. A total of 1,293 experts were invited to participate, and 442 (34%) completed at least the first page of questions, with 417 (94%) completing all mandatory questions. The survey also included optional sociodemographic questions and allowed respondents to provide additional suggestions. Quantitative and qualitative data analysis was conducted, with a partial completion cut-off set at more than 6% of mandatory questions. The findings informed the development of the WHO guideline on school health services, which aims to enhance transparency and provide evidence-based recommendations for SHS implementation globally.
